-2  Causes of Constipation
Lifestyle and Diet
Lack of fiber in diet
Low total calorie and fluid intake
Iron and calcium supplements
Lack of exercise
Immobility
Laxative abuse
Postponing urge to defecate
Dysmotility Disorders
Chronic intestinal pseudoobstruction
Hypothyroidism
Colonic inertia
Gastroparesis
Hirschprung disease
Chagas disease
Metabolic and endocrine abnormal-
ities such as diabetes
Neurologic Diseases
Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
Multiple sclerosis
Muscular dystrophy
Parkinson’s disease
Friedrich ataxia
Cerebral palsy
Para- or quadriplegia
Spinal cord injury
Cerebrovascular disease
Brain trauma
Pelvic Floor Disorders
Pregnancy
Dyssynergic defecation
Chronic Use of Opiates
Oncology patients
Chronic pain patients
Narcotic bowel syndrome
Other Gastrointestinal 
Disorders
Diseases of the upper gastrointes-
tinal tract
Diseases of the large bowel  
resulting in:
Failure of propulsion along the 
colon (colonic inertia)
Anorectal malformations or 
outlet obstruction
Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)
Anal fissure
Data from Andrews CN, Storr M: The pathophysiology of chronic 
constipation, Can J Gastroenterol 25(Suppl B):16B, 2011; Longstreth 
GF et al: Functional bowel disorders, Gastroenterology 130:1480, 2006; 
Schiller LR: Nutrients and constipation: cause or cure? Pract Gastroen-
terol 32:4, 2008.

Functional Constipation
